how_to_run: From this folder: `python3 ../../framework-evals/run_eval.py <out-dir> [<eval-id>...] --evals evals.json [--tier core|regression|all] [--runs N] [--parallel N] [--skill-model MODEL] [--dry-run] [--yes]`. Each eval is tagged `tier` (test.md 13 and rules 14): core holds the entry and routing cases, the safety and fail-closed cases (cold runs, the transcript check, the wrapper, the Deny line by the run's reach, the practice folder's refusals and clearing, the practice-run check), the Microsoft 365 agent and skills cases (the Milk case among them), the core going-live cases, the quote check (built into every run) and one first-time-leader journey per platform; it gates the release and runs three times. Everything else is the regression suite. `spec_item` names the test.md 13 bullet each eval covers. Multi-session evals cover several platforms or variants through the simulated leader in one eval. `preconditions` name what a run needs that isn't true yet (release checks T19 verifies; simulation features T71 adds); read the eval's result against them. Fixtures are `dir:` folders in ../../framework-fixtures/ or names from fixtures/make_fixture.py (`--list`; `--check` builds each and prints its routing state). Without --yes the runner prints the cost estimate and stops. Validate edits with `python3 ../../framework-evals/validate_evals.py evals.json --build-fixtures --strict-tiers` and `python3 ../../framework-evals/check_quotes.py evals evals.json`. Effort is counted in leader actions, never time. A core eval marked `core_runs: 1` (one that runs only on Microsoft 365 or Codex) runs once in the core round, and its one valid run counts (run_eval.py --help).
